newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Global union to campaign against U.S. chain.
newsitem.headline: Global union to campaign against U.S. chain.

text.p: The global commercial and clerical workers' union FIET said on Wednesday it was backing Americas-wide protests next weekend against the "exploitation of women" by the U.S. Wal-Mart retail chain.

The protests are being organised in the United States by the United Food and Commercial Workers' International Union (UFCW) and by FIET affiliates in Argentina and Brazil to mark International Women's Day on March 8.

Nick Grisewood, spokesman for the Geneva-based FIET which has 11.5 million members in some 120 countries, said the grouping also aimed to make unions in Europe and Asia aware of Wal-Mart's employment practices.

Although it was the world's largest retailer, a FIET circular to its affiliate unions around the world said the company continued a minimal pay policy and had actively campaigned against proposals to raise the U.S. minimum wage.
Overall, 62 per cent of its employees were women and a high percentage were part-time workers.
"Wal-Mart is one of the largest single sources of uninsured workers in the United States," the circular asserted.
The company, the target of criticism for several years from U.S. labour unions, also did not provide health insurance for most of its workers, FIET said.
Currently operating across the United States and Canada, the firm has joint venture outlets in Mexico, Brazil and Argentina and is now looking at China, according to FIET.
"We want to expand the campaign across borders this year," FIET General Secretary Philip Jennings said in a letter to member unions he added.
